messages:
tess: quick heads-up: discovered reproducible kv aliasing on orpheus-7b-int8 when prefill crosses 32768. minimal repro attached below.

marc: interesting — is it aliasing (wrap) or clamp? can you paste logs?

ida: repro snippet (single-threaded) and log:
```bash
# run_long_prefill.sh --model=orpheus-7b-int8 --prefill=33000 --trace=kv
# log lines:
kv.write req=32990 stored=32990
kv.write req=33001 stored=2
kv.read  req=33001 served=2
rotary.apply pos=33001 used=2
```

qa: reproduced locally on CPU build. looks like a modulo by 32768. my theory: one of the legacy typedefs (short) still used for slot index in the sharded backend.

marc: i remember a change last quarter that lifted SHARD_SZ to 65536 but kept some helper typedefs. i'll grep for uint16_t/short indices in kv/shard and fast-kernel.

ida: low-risk mitigation until patch: enable "kv.prefix-eviction" when prefill > 30k for canaries so we avoid writing high indices. that'll reduce audio/dialog quality for very long prompts but prevents silent aliasing.

marc: agreed. also adding an assert in dev builds that triggers if stored_pos != req_pos for >32k positions, with dump of last 64 writes. that'll make CI fail early.

tess: adding unit test that exercises indices [32760..32780] and [32800..33020] to catch both off-by-one and wrap. will open PR with test vectors and patch to change slot index to uint32_t.

devex-bot: CI triggered: kv-index-audit/patch-4160000000. Running unit-kernel-tests.

marc: once PR lands i'll run float vs int8 diff on the long-prefill goldset to confirm quality delta disappears. leaving notes here. :thumbsup:
